subject: Culture
title: Restorative Justice Circles
description: A 60-second lesson on Restorative Justice Circles.

hook.text: In New Zealand, a teenage offender sits in a circle with the victim's family and together they design the punishment.

buildup.text: Restorative justice comes from Māori 'hui' traditions where crime is a wound to the whole community.

discovery.text: Offenders who face their victims directly show 27% lower reoffending rates than those who go through courts.

twist.text: Traditional Western justice asks 'What law was broken?' Restorative justice asks 'Who was harmed and how?'

climax.text: Rwanda used 'gacaca' village courts to process over a million genocide cases in a decade.

punchline.text: Healing needs faces, not just files.

quiz.question: What indigenous tradition inspired New Zealand's restorative justice model?

details.summary: Restorative justice circles — where offenders face their victims in facilitated dialogue — offer an alternative to both revenge justice and impersonal courts.
details.whyItMatters: Restorative justice represents a third path between honor-based revenge and guilt-based punishment. It suggests that honor can be restored through dialogue and accountability rather than violence or imprisonment.
takeaways: Maori family group conferences inspired New Zealand's juvenile justice reforms
Restorative justice reduces reoffending rates by 25-30% in studies
South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission applied restorative principles

faq.question: How do restorative justice circles work?
faq.answer: The offender, victim, their families, and community members sit in a circle facilitated by a trained mediator. The victim describes the harm's impact. The offender must listen, acknowledge responsibility, and participate in creating a repair plan (community service, restitution, behavioral.

faq.question: Does restorative justice actually work?
faq.answer: Research consistently shows restorative justice reduces reoffending by 25-30% compared to conventional courts. Victim satisfaction is significantly higher — victims report feeling heard and healed rather than re-traumatized.
